alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Glomeruli are tufts of capillaries arranged in rows on either side of an interlobular artery in the convoluted portion of the cortex. Each capillary is supplied by an afferent arteriole. The renal corpuscle consists of the glomerulus and the surrounding Bowman's capsule, which is technically a component of the renal tubule.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The medullary ray, located in the cortex, forms the center of the renal lobule and consists of the straight portions of the proximal and distal tubules and the collecting ducts. Convoluted portions of the cortex are located between medullary rays and contain the renal corpuslces and the convoluted portions of the tubules.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Podocytes form the visceral layer of Bowman's capsule and lie directly on the basal lamina of the endothelial cells of the glomerulus. Podocytes can be distinguished from endothelial cells because they face Bowman's space, rather than the lumen of the capillary.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Bowman's capsule is the expanded beginning of the renal tubule. It is indented by the glomerulus, thereby forming two layers, with Bowman's space between them. The visceral layer is composed of podocytes which lie on the basal lamina of the endothelial cells of the glomerulus. The parietal layer contacts the parenchyma of the kidney.

Distal tubules are distinguished from proximal tubules by their low cuboidal epithelium, the irregular placement of nuclei around the lumen, and lack of a brush border. This is a convoluted portion of the distal tubule tubule because it is in the convoluted portion of the kidney, as indicated by the presence of renal corpuscles.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The renal cortex is that region of the kidney above the arcuate vessels. It is subdivided into convoluted portions, that contain the glomeruli and convoluted tubules, and medullary ray portions, which contain straight tubules and collecting ducts.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Renal pyramids are subdivisions of the renal medulla that contain portions of the renal tubules, portions of the collecting ducts, and the ducts of Bellini. Renal pyramids project into the renal pelvis where they are covered by a minor calyx. The tip of the pyramid is termed the papilla.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The macula densa is a group of specialized cells that cluster in the wall of the distal convoluted tubule. The macula densa, along with adjacent, specialized smooth muscle cells in the wall of the afferent arteriole, form the juxtaglomerular apparatus.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The afferent arteriole supplies the glomerulus and can only be positively identified when it is seen as part of the juxtaglomerular complex, as seen here. The afferent arteriole is larger than the efferent arteriole, and this size differential results in elevated blood pressure in the glomerulus, thereby aiding in the formation of the glomerular filtrate.
